verdict.what: Return the terrainHeightTools API if the THT module is active, otherwise null
verdict.helper: thtApi() — no parameters, returns globalThis.terrainHeightTools or null
verdict.notes: Identical three-line bodies; extracting to a shared module-level helper removes the duplication cleanly. Ensure THT_ID constant is accessible from the shared location.

verdict.what: same name but completely different implementations checking isometric mode
verdict.notes: iso-elevation-anim.js does a full multi-step check (module active, world setting, scene flag), while token-ruler.js delegates to a provider abstraction. These are not the same logic — one is the concrete implementation, the other may use a different/newer abstraction. Merging them risks breaking one of the two callers or forcing an inappropriate coupling between files with different dependency structures.

verdict.what: guard-then-create two PIXI containers and attach a sin-wave alpha ticker
verdict.notes: Structural similarity is superficial. The ticker callbacks diverge significantly: shape-placement-engine only pulses alpha on two containers and cleans up two variables, while target-shapes iterates _persistShapes/_persistLabels, calls paintShape/updateLabel per token per tick, and clears four extra collections on teardown. Container attachment also differs (addGraphicsBelowTokens/addGraphicsAboveTokens vs. canvas.stage.addChild with eventMode). A shared helper would need to accept callbacks for attachment, per-tick work, and cleanup — producing an abstraction more complex than the two originals. The shared alpha formula (0.65 + 0.35 * Math.sin(performance.now() / 280)) is the only truly identical line, but extracting a one-liner constant adds no real value.

verdict.what: both named `hide` but do entirely different things in different domains
verdict.notes: Name collision only. One removes a tooltip DOM node; the other tears down a PIXI debug container and unhooks Foundry hooks. Different domains, different logic, different state. No shared abstraction is possible or useful.

verdict.what: Guard on globalThis.terrainHeightTools, convert pixel coords to grid offset, return getHexGroundElevation(j, i) || 0
verdict.notes: The only real differences are (1) the anim file destructures x/y into a point literal — trivially unified to accept a point object — and (2) the anim version wraps in try/catch while the ruler version does not. The shared helper should include the try/catch (the safer default), and the iso-elevation-anim call site simply passes { x, y } instead of the two separate args. Both files already live in scripts/movement/, so a shared movement-utils module keeps cohesion tight.

verdict.what: both are named `show` but do completely unrelated things: one renders a tooltip DOM element, the other initializes a PIXI debug overlay
verdict.notes: Same function name, entirely different domains (DOM tooltip vs. Foundry/PIXI debug visualization). No shared logic, no shared types, no shared abstractions possible.

verdict.what: Look up ISO provider for a token, check isTokenDisabled, and return the {reverseRotation, reverseSkewX, reverseSkewY, counterScale} object (or null)
verdict.notes: The feature-enabled guard differs between the two sites (one uses isIsoFeatureEnabled(), the other uses game.settings.get with a try/catch), so each call site keeps its own guard and calls getIsoStateForToken only after passing it. The helper encapsulates only the shared tail: provider lookup, isTokenDisabled check, and object construction.

verdict.what: both are `_onCreateToken` hook handlers but do entirely different things
verdict.notes: Same lifecycle hook name, different domains: one handles detection mode augmentation and sight range settings on token creation; the other builds edge vision sources. No shared logic exists beyond the hook signature.

verdict.what: Injecting a form-group into the token config vision tab
verdict.notes: Same hook, same tab target, same append+resize pattern — but the injected UI is completely different (checkbox vs. select), the flag semantics differ (boolean vs. on/off/default), and the jQuery normalization differs slightly. The shared scaffold (find tab, get tokenDoc flag, append block, setPosition) is only ~5 lines of boilerplate around very different domain logic. Factoring would require parameterising the inner HTML block, the flag read/transform, and the tooltip — producing an abstraction more complex than either original. Not worth it.

verdict.what: Cube-coordinate rounding for hex grids (identical 9-line algorithm)
verdict.notes: Bodies are byte-for-byte identical. Extract to a shared hex-utils module and import in both files. The fallback name in hex-drag-stabilizer suggests it was copied precisely because the shared version wasn't accessible at the time.
